messages:
mike-platform: Quick question — when a dedicated tenant spills to hosted, do we require explicit customer consent in the console, or is that implied by their dedicated contract? I'm leaning toward an opt-in toggle + audit event. cc @anya-ops @sarah-ml

anya-ops: we should treat regulated customers differently. proposal: default to blocking spillover unless tenant has 'allow_hosted_fallback' set to true in the console. that way orgs can opt in. also emit an audit log + webhook. :lock:

anya-ops: example console flag (UI + API) — here's a rough snippet we could use server-side for the control: 
```json
{
  "tenant_id": "T-1234",
  "allow_hosted_fallback": false,
  "fallback_policy": "reject|notify|allow-with-variant",
  "fallback_variant": "open-compat-v1-quant"
}
```

sarah-ml: agree on opt-in. also need pre-fallback quality check for the variant. we should run a quick eval against a tenant-specific prompt set or at least check last-30d drift metric before routing to a lower-quality variant. add tag `fallback_quality_passed` to telemetry.

jordan-oncall: important: when fallback happens we need immediate incident-level telemetry: `routing.fallback.count` + `routing.fallback.latency_delta` + `tenant.impact=true/false`. want to wire a PagerDuty signal if fallback increases error% or latency beyond threshold in 5m window.

mike-platform: thanks. do we have a proposed UX copy? Legal/privacy will want explicit language. maybe: "Allow Redwood to route requests to hosted infrastructure when Dedicated capacity is unavailable. This may route requests to a model variant hosted outside your VPC." toggle + learn more modal.

anya-ops: that copy works. let's also expose reason history in the tenant timeline: show events like `fallback_attempted`, `fallback_succeeded`, `fallback_rejected` with timestamps and variant used. audit event name: `tenant.routing.fallback`.

sarah-ml: telemetry detail: include `fallback_variant`, `model_family`, `variant_quant`, `decision_reason` (e.g., capacity_shortage, region_unavailable, priority_evict). Metrics should be tagged with `customer_tier` so we can roll up to enterprise vs free.

jordan-oncall: for SLOs: keep automatic fallback allowed but apply soft-throttles (eg degrade concurrency per-tenant when on hosted variant) to protect hosted capacity. and log `throttle_applied=true`. If a tenant's requests are throttled repeatedly, surface to account owners + SE.

mike-platform: implementation questions for the internal routing API: should the router return a single decision object or a list of candidates? I prefer single decision + `alternatives[]` for debug. something like:
```json
{
  "route": "hosted",
  "reason": "dedicated_exhausted",
  "variant": "open-compat-v1-quant",
  "alternatives": ["dedicated-pool-3","hosted-compat-v2"]
}
```

anya-ops: alternatives are useful for debugging only. they must not leak capacity details to customers. wire them to internal-only logs and redact in public APIs.

console-bot: feature-flag created: `tenant.allow_hosted_fallback` (staging:true dev:true prod:false). created Jira EPIC PF-492 for rollout + audit schema.

mike-platform: next steps: 1) add API flag + console toggle (anya) 2) telemetry + metrics (sarah/jordan) 3) router returns decision + internal alternatives (platform infra) 4) legal copy review (me). I'll draft a small RFC and assign tasks. anyone object?

sarah-ml: sgtm — I'll add the eval/gating check to the RFC so fallback only kicks in if `fallback_quality_passed=true` or tenant explicitly allows risk.

anya-ops: fine by me. will start the console mock and update PF-492 with UI screenshots. :white_check_mark:

jordan-oncall: will add alert runbook + PD escalation rules to the epic.

mike-platform: cool — thanks all. I'll post the RFC link when ready. :eyes:
